I don't care if you traveled with the President herself. Rules are rules. Now leave before I have you escorted out. ...Wait. And who exactly is your father supposed to be?
My father is Dr. Thrun! He worked for the Republic! He's smarter than all of you combined!

Officer! What is going on here? Are you really giving her trouble just because she's a girl? I'm a girl too. Do you have a problem with me as well? Dr. Thrun's daughter right? I knew your father. He was a good man. Officer, she stays. She will be my guest.
Recruit! You heard Miss Pawn. However, you brought the girl here so she is your responsibility. If anything happens to her, you will be disciplined. Now get moving.
training_officer_speech: Listen up, recruits! You are here because you have chosen to serve something greater than yourselves. You will fight for what belongs to us: our lands, our freedom, our people. We will never bow to an imposed tyrant whose only goal is conquest. The road ahead will not be easy. But if you survive what comes next, you will earn the right to call yourselves soldiers of the Republic. Now move! Twenty laps around the camp! Go, go, go!

No way... is that you? Do you remember me? Cynian Rain! Ha! I remember you could barely keep up with the other kids back in the village and now you want to be a soldier? You should have trained a bit before showing up here. Well, at least you'll make me look good by comparison. Just know that I intend to rise through the ranks. And I won't let anything get in my way. Try to keep up.

Hey, don't listen to her. We'll see how the skinny ones do when they run out of supplies on a mission. Us on the other hand? We've got reserves for days, haha. The name's Badol. Badol Decisive. I heard you were recommended by Major Arthur himself. That's no small thing. Don't worry, we'll get through this together.

If you're done introducing yourselves! It is time for the real test. Every year, hundreds enlist only because they want food, shelter, and the comfort that being a soldier provides. The army cannot afford to keep those who are not truly committed. By tomorrow, only a handful of you will remain. The rest will be on their way back home. You will complete three tasks.

First: I want to see the remains of five Sinkers. Bring me proof that you can handle Imperial Zoids. Second: obtain the Zi-Data from a Gorgodos. Intelligence and data collection are as important as combat. Third: you will present your Zoid before me. A soldier must keep their Zoids in top condition and ready for battle. I don't want to see weak, underfed Zoids in my ranks. You have your orders. Dismissed.
training_officer_trials_done: Well, well. Who would have thought, you actually finished. You arrived long after everyone else. That friend of yours, Rain, was the first to complete the tasks. And you were supposed to be the one recommended by a Major? Ha. But you made it. Many have already packed their things and left. Now only the true soldiers remain. You have earned the right to stay. Prepare yourself for the real training.
kara_companion_imperial: Your father was a difficult man to understand, but his work saved more lives than most people know. I met him years ago, before the war consumed everything. He was brilliant, stubborn, and deeply kind beneath all that coldness. He would be proud to see you standing here.
You may stay here under our protection, Kara. But remember, this is still a military camp.
And you must be the new recruit. I am Lieutenant Kirsche Hartriegel. Take care of this girl. She is stronger than she looks.

How did it go? I was talking to Lieutenant Kirsche. I was curious and started exploring the camp on my own. I wandered somewhere I was not supposed to be and a soldier was about to scold me. Then she showed up and told him to leave me alone.

We started talking and she recognized me. She said she knew my father. Can you believe that? She has been very kind to me. I did not expect that from Imperial soldiers. They are different from what I imagined.
But I still do not understand this war. Both sides seem to believe they are right. I just hope we are fighting for the right reasons.
kara_companion: You look tired. I've been with Mana these days. She taught me a lot about Zoids. Things I never knew. She even let me see some of my father's old research. He really was working on something important here.

Everyone here talks about freedom and justice. But the Republic is fighting a war on a continent that isn't even theirs. And they refuse to back down. How is that so different from what the Empire does? Both sides are to blame for this war, each in their own way. But I hope you'll be different. I hope you joined for the right reasons.
cynian_rain_companion: Oh, hanging out with a little girl? Can't handle girls your own age? Ha! Hi there, I'm Cynian Rain. And you are...?
I'm Kara. And I'm not a little girl. So you're from the village too? Yeah, we sure are fools in Gleam. Joining a war that isn't even ours just for glory...

I'm not here for glory! Do you remember the food shortages? The hunger, the empty markets? That was all because of the Empire. It all started when they decided they had the right to settle on this continent. They took our resources, dragged our people away, and left villages like ours to starve. They should have stayed in Nyx where they belong. I won't rest until they pay for what they did. That's why I'm here. And if you're smart, neither of you will get in my way.
badol_decisive_companion: Hey! How are you holding up? You made it through the trials, that's what matters. Oh, and who is this? Your little sister? You know, I have a brother about your age back home. Maybe I should introduce you two, haha!
I'm not his sister! My name is Kara! And... W-What!? Ugh, you're just as annoying as him! I should have expected nothing less from a thick-headed soldier who only knows how to fight.

Hahaha! I'm just messing with you. And I'm not here just to fight or for glory. Back in my village, there's barely any food or work. Everything is scarce. Joining the army was my only real option. At least this way I can send money back to my family.

Why the Republic? Well, they control the central continent. More land, more resources, more opportunities. And I wouldn't want to live in Nyx even if they paid me, haha! I heard even the Zoids there are depressed. So here I am. Not the most heroic reason, but it's an honest one. And it's a sacrifice I'm willing to make for my old lady back home.
imperial_officer_ruins_briefing: Listen up, recruits. Intelligence has located an artifact in ruins north of the camp. A reconnaissance team already mapped the area. The ruins are under Imperial Sleeper control, so resistance should be minimal.
You three will join a squad of soldiers heading to the site. Your job is simple: recover the artifact and bring it back. Think of it as your first real assignment.

Crescent, keep your temper in check. Hawk, use that speed of yours for something other than running away. And you, you like Sleepers, right? You will feel right at home. Like a dysfunctional family reunion.
Do not overthink it. Get in, get the artifact, get out. The veterans will handle the heavy work. Do not get in their way.
rhine_hawk_pre_ruins: So this is it. Our first real mission. I have been looking at the area and it seems straightforward enough. Narrow passages, open chambers. As long as we stay together, we should be fine.

I know my Merda is not the strongest Zoid out there. But she is fast. Back in Nyx, speed was all that mattered. You did not want to be exposed to the cold any longer than you had to. This girl has gotten us out of trouble more times than I can count.
If things go sideways, I can scout ahead or draw attention away. That is what she is built for. Quick in, quick out.
Let us make it back in one piece, alright?
eddie_crescent_pre_ruins: A recovery mission. They are sending us to pick up some dusty artifact from a bunch of ruins full of sleeping Zoids. What an incredible use of my talents.
You know what this is, right? They do not trust us with anything real yet. So they give us the errands. Go fetch this, bring back that. Like we are delivery boys.

Sure, the Iguan is a basic Zoid. But that is exactly the point. It is the perfect machine to prove what a real pilot can do. I can squeeze more out of one Iguan than you can out of that whole junk mob of Sleepers you drag around. How are you not bored out of your mind waiting for those things to actually do something?
Just try to keep up out there. I do not plan on babysitting both of you.
narration_ruins_discovery: Guysacks! Guysacks everywhere! These are not ours! Since when are there Republican Sleepers in this area?!
I do not see any of the soldiers! Where is the rest of the squad?!
Are you deaf?! Forget the soldiers! The sand is moving under your feet and you two are just standing there like idiots on a field trip!
We have gone too deep into the desert. These Zoids are hiding underground. We cannot see them until they are already on top of us.
Yeah, no kidding! The ruins, now! The corridors are narrow enough to keep them from flanking us. Unless you geniuses want to stay out here and get torn apart!
And what if the soldiers never show up?!
Then congratulations, we are on our own! Now shut up and move! And you, use that junk pile of Sleepers you carry around to hold them off, or have you gotten attached to those things too?!
narration_ruins_aftermath: Wait... those are Imperial uniforms. The soldiers... they are all dead.
Every single one of them. They were cut down before they even reached the inner chambers.
This was a trap. The whole thing. The Sleepers outside were herding us in here. Think about it. They did not chase us, they surrounded us. They pushed us toward the ruins on purpose.
But Sleepers have never behaved like that before. They do not coordinate. They just sit and wait.
Exactly. The Republic must be testing some new tactic and we walked right into their proving ground. These are not normal Sleepers anymore. They have been reprogrammed to hunt.
My equipment has been picking up strange readings since we got inside. Some kind of wave interference. It is not random. It is coming from below. Something down there is jamming our communications.
Look at the soldiers. They were heading toward that passage. It leads down, probably to a well or a shaft. The readings match. Whatever is down there is the source of the interference.
Then we go down. We still have a mission to complete. The artifact should be there. Let us finish this and get out.
narration_guysack_appears: This is it. The water has flooded part of the chamber. The artifact must be somewhere below the surface.
One of the soldiers left a recon pod near the entrance. It is small enough to navigate the flooded section.

Hawk, you take the pod. Your Merda is useless down there and I do not trust this one's Sleepers anywhere near something valuable. Besides, have you seen the size of that pod? There is no way this one fits in there.
Fine. But you two better keep things quiet up here while I am down there.
Get ready. I hear something. The ground is shaking.
What the... look at the size of that thing! That must be the one coordinating the others. Look at the signal array on its back. It is the command unit. That is why the Sleepers were organized.
What is going on up there?! I can hear rumbling!
I hope those Sleepers of yours are at least good enough to serve as a snack for that thing. Rhine is still down there. If you want to save her, you will have to stop it. Good luck.
What?! Eddie!! EDDIE!! He abandoned us! You have to hold it off! I am almost done down here! Please, do not leave me too!
narration_eddie_returns: I got the artifact! I am coming up! What is happening up th...
What is that thing?! It is enormous! And Eddie... Eddie that coward left us!
More Sleepers are coming from the corridors! We are surrounded!
An explosion tore through the ceiling above the giant Guysack. Rubble and stone rained down, pinning the beast to the ground. From a breach in the upper level, the Iguan stood covered in dust.
What kind of soldier would I be if I cannot even save a couple of good-for-nothings like you?
That will not hold it for long. Hawk, your Merda is the only thing fast enough to outrun the horde heading this way. I already cleared a passage to the west corridor.
And you, protect her on the way out. Do not stop for anything. I will hold this thing here.
Eddie, you cannot stay! When it gets back up...
I said go! There is no time! It is already moving!
narration_rhine_plan: We cannot leave him! But there are too many! What do we do?! Eddie... are we really going to abandon him? We cannot do anything!
What? Use your Sleepers? But the signals are jammed! We cannot reach them from...
Wait. You are right. If we get close enough, the interference will not be as strong. The signal could get through.

Alright, here is the plan. You program the Sleeper module with instructions to scatter through the tunnels. I take it on my Merda and get close enough to each of your Zoids to make sure the signal reaches them. The Republican Sleepers will chase them.

You go back to Eddie. While the horde spreads out chasing your Sleepers, maybe the three of us will have a chance to take down the leader together. It is risky, but it is our only option. Program the module. Let us go!
narration_eddie_reunite: What the hell are you doing here?! I told you to run! Nobody asked for your help!
Whatever. If you want to die, that thing over there can help you with that. Its armor is too thick. I have been hitting it and I cannot do any real damage.

Fine. If we are doing this, you had better be useful. Look at the transmitters on its back. It is the only spot that is exposed. They cannot cover it or it would dampen the signal. If we have any chance, we concentrate our fire there.
And try not to die. I did not clear half this ruin just to watch you get crushed at the end.
narration_eddie_resolve: I made it! The horde is scattered!
You too, huh. Fine, at least you are good for something. Distract it while I reposition. This time we will not miss.
NOW! This is our chance! Hit the transmitters!
Both pilots fired at the exposed point on the Guysack's back. A massive explosion tore through its abdomen, sending pieces of armor flying across the chamber.
It is down! We did it!
Do not celebrate yet. The horde will not stay scattered forever. We have a window. Move, now!
We actually made it. All three of us.
Save the sentimentality for later. Let us get out of here before anything else crawls out of the sand. And nobody talks about this back at camp. Understood?
imperial_officer_ruins_debrief: Before anything else, I owe you an apology. Intelligence failed us. I never intended to put fresh cadets in that kind of danger.
However, you three survived a mission where many seasoned soldiers did not. That speaks volumes about your abilities.
I have reviewed the field report. You showed real leadership out there. Coordinating under pressure, adapting to a situation no one anticipated. That takes more than skill. That takes instinct.
Thank you, sir. But I put Cadet Hawk in danger. And I would never have made it out without this one's Sleepers. I am not ready to lead anything yet.
Ha! That is exactly the kind of answer I want to hear from a soldier. The ones who think they are ready are usually the first to fall.
Get some rest, all of you. You have earned it.
narration_team_bonding: You blew up the ceiling of ancient ruins?! Wow!
Yeah! You should have seen this idiot's face when I came through. Standing right under it looking confused while a giant Guysack was about to eat them alive.
Oh sure, because we were already fighting that thing before you even showed up, Eddie.
Ha! Right, right. They thought I had abandoned them. You should have seen their faces when I dropped through the ceiling.
But the shot, Kara. You should have seen it. Both of them firing at the same spot at the exact same time.
If it had been anyone else pulling that trigger instead of me, you would all be dead. I am not even sure this one actually hit anything.
You really fought all those Sleepers by yourself just to clear a path for them?
Someone had to, kid. These two were too busy panicking. Actually, on my way out I saw a Guysack so confused it was slapping the others around. Even they could not believe what was happening.
Eddie... I owe you an apology. When I saw your Iguan leaving, I thought the worst. I judged you and I was wrong. You risked your life for us. That took real courage.

Do not get sentimental on me, Hawk. I did what needed to be done. Although I will say, you are faster than I thought. That Merda of yours really moved out there. Without your speed, the plan would have fallen apart.
Wait... did Eddie just compliment someone?
I am stating a fact! Her Zoid is fast. That is not a compliment, that is basic observation!
You know what? All of you can shut up. Next mission, I am going alone. Less idiots to worry about.
imperial_officer_escort_briefing: Good, you are all here. I have a new assignment. This one requires discretion.
We have a contact operating in Republican territory. A transporter. Not military, not loyal to anyone, but willing to move a shipment of explosives for us.
Your mission is to escort the contact to where the explosives are stored. Once the cargo is secured, the transporter will handle the rest.
You will be crossing into enemy territory. Avoid confrontation at all costs. Get in, find the contact, get the cargo, and come back without drawing attention.
companions_pre_escort: This is completely different from the ruins. We are crossing into enemy territory. We need to stay away from cities and main roads. We will go through the desert and keep our Zoids hidden to avoid suspicion.
Great. Now we are babysitters for some smuggler we cannot even recognize. Just when I thought the missions were getting better.
Speaking of babysitting, what are you doing here, kid?
Kirsche gave me permission to come with you! She said you were not planning to engage anyone, so it should be safe.

Also, how are we supposed to know who the contact is? What does a transporter even look like? We should watch out either way. People who work for both sides are not loyal to anyone. The moment things go bad, they will think about themselves first.
And how exactly are we supposed to go unnoticed with this one's entire circus of Sleepers following behind? We might as well carry a banner that says 'shoot here'.
narration_bar_investigation: Porto Nido. If there is a transporter working this coast, someone in this town will know about it.
The officer gave us a pass phrase. 'I have something that needs to be moved tonight.' Whoever responds with the right answer is our contact.
That is the most idiotic pass phrase I have ever heard. Who writes these? Fine, let us get this over with.
Let us just say it to whoever looks like a transporter around the docks.
I am NOT saying that. You do it, Hawk.
Fine, I will do it. Excuse me, sir? I have something that needs to be moved... tonight.
Something that needs to be moved tonight? I will move whatever you want, as many times as you want, sweetheart.
Oh! Are you the... wait, what are you doing? Let go of my arm!
Come on, do not be shy. You came to me, remember? Boys, make sure she feels welcome.
Go! Find her! I will deal with these idiots!
narration_rhine_rescue: Let go of me! I said LET GO!
Keep struggling, sweetheart. Makes it more fun. Throw her in the Zoid. We are taking her with us.
We have to save her! Forget about being discovered, we deal with that later!
Boss! Someone is coming! They have got Zoids!
Tch. Of course there are more of them. Get to your machines!
narration_rhine_rescued: ...Thank you. If you had not shown up...
I am fine. I am fine. Let us just... go back and see if Eddie is okay.
About time you showed up. I was running out of people to hit.
I have had worse. Listen, I got something from the bartender. Turns out our transporter is not here. She operates near the Tauros Grotto.
He was very eager to share once I explained that I would break his bar a second time if he did not.
Then we head to the Grotto. Let us go. We are already discovered, so much for discretion.
narration_arrive_tauros: This is the Tauros Grotto. The bartender said our contact operates around here somewhere.
Great. Another hole in the ground. Because the last time we went underground it went so well for us.
I am just saying. Every time we go underground, something tries to kill us. Maybe I should just wait out here until you start screaming like cowards.
Let us look around. Stay alert.
moonbay_intro: Hey! What is all this noise? I was down here looking for treasure and you lot come stomping in like you own the place.
Who the hell are you? You do not look like the usual scavengers.
We could ask you the same thing. What are you doing in caves this close to a war zone?
War zone? These caves do not belong to anyone. I go where the money is.

Wait. That is an Iguan out there. And a Merda. Those are Imperial Zoids. You are soldiers from the Empire, in Republican territory. This does not concern me, but if you do not leave right now, I am calling my Republic contacts. They pay well for information about trespassers.
I have something that needs to be moved tonight.
I cannot believe it! Someone actually said it! YOU are my contact?! The Empire sent a bunch of kids and a little girl said the phrase! Hahahaha!

I am Moonbay. I wrote that phrase on purpose. The whole point was that no real army would ever use something that embarrassing as a code. So no military patrol would ever come looking for me using it. Only my real contact would be desperate enough to say it out loud!
moonbay_getting_to_know: Hahaha! So you actually said the phrase to some thugs at Porto Nido?! And they thought... hahaha!
It was NOT funny, Moonbay. They grabbed me. It was bad.

Okay, sorry. But you know I designed that phrase to be as embarrassing as possible, right? If it sounds like something a real soldier would say, patrols could stumble into it. But something that stupid? Only my real contact would ever say it.
It worked, did it not? Here you are. Now, where is the pickup point? I was only told to meet my escort here.
Arcobaleno Camp. Command is using it as a hidden supply cache now that the bandits are gone.
An abandoned bandit camp as a weapons cache? Clever. Let us move. You handle the fighting, I handle the transport.
narration_arcobaleno_ambush: This is the place. But something is wrong. The guards should be here.
Look. Imperial soldiers. Dead. The camp was raided.
Are you kidding me?! Who uses an abandoned bandit camp to hide military supplies?! Of course someone else moved in! Command is full of geniuses!
The cargo is gone. Some other group must have taken over the camp after the previous bandits were driven out.
Wait. The cargo has tracking devices. Standard Imperial protocol for high-value shipments. If the explosives are still in one piece, we should be able to pick up the signal.
Finally, someone thought of something useful. Where are they?
The signal is split. They divided the cargo and went in different directions. We will have to track down each group to recover everything.
Of course they did. Nothing is ever simple. Let us move.
moonbay_pickup_1: So, you are the Sleeper pilot they keep talking about. I have seen a lot of pilots, but never one who drags around an army of sleeping Zoids. How does that even work?
Most people use one Zoid. Maybe two. You just... collect them? Like pets?
They are not pets! They are...
Hey, I am not judging. Whatever gets the job done. I once transported a guy who fought with three Molgas strapped to a trailer. You are not the weirdest client I have had.
Hold on. You. The girl. What is your name? You look familiar somehow.
Thrun?! As in Doctor Thrun? I have heard of him. He is famous among transporters. Always moving research equipment to weird places nobody wants to go.
I know OF him. Never met him personally. But his shipments always paid well. What is he up to these days?
I... do not know. I have not seen him in a long time.
Oh. Sorry, kid. Did not mean to... anyway, what is that thing following you around? That little creature.
This is Beacon! I am not sure what he is exactly. But he is my friend and he has saved me more than once.

It is not a Zoid, that is for sure. I have seen a lot of machines in my line of work. That thing is something else entirely. You should be careful with it. Something that rare tends to attract the wrong kind of attention.
moonbay_pickup_2: So let me see if I have this right. The angry one with the Iguan tried to sacrifice himself to save you all? Who would have guessed. Maybe he likes you.
I did NOT sacrifice myself! I was repositioning! And I do NOT like anyone!
Sure you do not, kid. You just charged into a bar full of thugs to save your friend. Total coincidence.
She is not my friend! She is a fellow soldier! There is a difference!
Mhm. And the girl with the weird creature, the pilot with the sleeping army, and mister 'I do not have friends'... you know, for a bunch of Imperial soldiers, you are actually not that bad.
Coming from someone who would sell us out for the right price, I will take that as a compliment.
Smart boy. Now let us go get the next shipment.
narration_desert_gorge_reflection: That was the last one. All three shipments recovered.
You know, after hearing all your stories... you all joined the Empire for real reasons. Not for glory or power. To protect the people you love.
But I have been on both sides of this war. The Republic's soldiers? They say the same things you do. Their reasons are not wrong either.
Your reasons are not wrong. But the war is. Good people killing good people because of 'noble reasons'. That is what war really is.
I do not pick sides because I have seen what sides do to people. Just... do not lose yourselves in this. Fight for your reasons, not for their flags.
Mission complete. We delivered the cargo. Now she does her part.
One last favor? I need an escort through Elmia Ruins. With this much cargo, I cannot defend myself if something jumps me in there. After that, I am out of your hair.
Consider it a bonus round. Otherwise I will charge the Empire extra and tell them it was because you refused to finish the job.
narration_moonbay_farewell: Well, this is where we part ways. Cargo is secure, path is clear. I can handle it from here.
Will we see you again, Moonbay?
Who knows, kid? But this was not the worst job I have ever had. Take care of yourself. And that creature of yours, do not let the wrong people find out about it.
And you. Take good care of your two girls out there.
T-two girls?! What is THAT supposed to mean?!
Haha! Look at that, she is turning red. I knew it.
I am NOT...! The heat! It is the desert!
Sure it is. Just like Eddie's excuse.
Anyway. Tell your bosses Moonbay delivers. Always. See you around, kids. And do me a favor, try not to move too many things tonight. You know how that turns out.
imperial_officer_escort_debrief: I have received confirmation from our contact. The transporter has the cargo and is en route to the delivery point. The mission was a success.
I heard about the incident at Porto Nido. You drew attention. That was not part of the plan.
But the mission is complete, and that is what matters. You have proven you can handle a life-or-death situation and a tedious escort mission equally well. That shows versatility.
Lieutenant Hartriegel has been observing your progress. I will let her take it from here.
Colonel Schwarz needs capable soldiers at the Red River. You three are to report there for deployment under his command.
Red River? That is a frontline deployment...
It is. And it is exactly where soldiers like you are needed. The Colonel does not accept just anyone. Consider this recognition of what you have accomplished.
Report to Red River when you are ready. I will arrange the transfer. Dismissed.
narration_post_escort_talk: Red River! Under Schwarz himself! This is it. This is where I prove what I am really worth. No more fetch missions, no more babysitting cargo. Real combat.
Eddie, do you even know what is happening at Red River? It is a ceasefire zone. Both armies are stationed on opposite sides. One wrong move and the whole thing erupts.
And what, you are scared? When things go bad, and they will, they are going to need soldiers like me. Not crybabies like you two.
Moonbay was... interesting. I did not expect to like her.
She was a transporter, Eddie. There is a difference.
She works for whoever pays. Today it is us, tomorrow it is the Republic. You cannot trust people like that.
Maybe. But what she said about the war... about both sides thinking they are right...
Fine. Whatever. Red River is what matters now. Schwarz wants soldiers, not philosophers. Let us be ready.
Kirsche has told me about Schwarz... a lot. He is an extraordinary pilot, strict but also reasonable and fair. She says he is one of the few officers who actually cares about his soldiers.
Good. Then maybe we will finally have a commander who knows what they are doing.
thug_bar: What do you want? You do not look like you belong here. Order something or get out.
badol_decisive_pre_ruins: A supply depot and some ruins? I thought being a soldier would be more glamorous. My mother is going to be disappointed.
But hey, orders are orders. As long as they keep paying me, I will keep showing up. My Guysack and I are ready for whatever.
I do not care how we win. I care about going home. And if this new system gets us there faster, I am all for it.
And relax, will you? You look like someone asked you to cook your own pet. We are just downloading an update on them, that is all. I got your back.
badol_post_ambush: Hey. I know that look. I get it.
I did not enjoy it. You know me better than that. But I was not going to let some mercenary ruin this mission. Too much depends on it.
Besides, I saved you the decision. And the fight with Rain. Did you see her out there? She would have torn you apart.
We are good, yeah? Come on. We still have ruins to clear.
badol_return_from_ruins: I am not going to lie, your Sleepers scared me back there. The way they moved, all at once... I do not want to be on the wrong side of that.
But you know what I keep thinking about? What Rain said. About losing her family because of the Empire.
I joined this war to feed mine. If someone took them from me... I would probably be just as furious as her.
Rain, you there? Can we talk?
Listen. Both of you. What happened in those ruins stays in those ruins. We do not talk about it at camp. Not to the officer, not to anyone.

And sort this out between you. Because if we are not a team, we are dead. And I did not leave my family behind just to die because my squadmates cannot stand each other. My mother is not burying her son over this. Are we clear?
That mercenary. The one who said he had kids. You think he was telling the truth?
...Do not think about it, Badol. Let us just get back to camp.
cynian_rain_pre_ruins: Finally, a real mission. I was getting tired of training drills. Time to smash some Imperial junk.
So that is what your Sleepers are for. Setting traps. I would rather look the enemy in the eye when I take them down, but I guess everyone fights how they can.
New technology or not, all I care about is that it hurts the Empire. If it works, it works. Simple as that.
Try to keep up out there. My Stealth Viper does not wait for anyone.
kara_pre_ruins: ...More effective? What do you mean, more effective?
More lethal. That is what you are saying. They want to turn my father's research into a better killing machine.
He created the Sleeper Module so Zoids could think for themselves. So they could choose. And now they are turning them into... this.
You knew. You knew the armies would do this with his work. And you still joined them. You still put on that uniform.
Just go! Go do your mission! I do not want to see you!
narration_badol_kill: The Sea Panther collapsed. The mercenary crawled out of the wreckage and tried to run, but there was nowhere to go. Cornered.
Please! If they capture me, they will hang me! Mercenaries get no trial, no rights! It is just a job! I did not choose this!
What are you waiting for?! Tie him up already!
I have a family! I have kids! I was just following orders! You are soldiers, you understand that, right?! You know what it is like!
Are you serious right now?! He is a mercenary! He just tried to kill us! Just restrain him and let command deal with it!
Look at me! I am unarmed! I am no threat to anyone! Just let me go and I disappear! You will never see me again, I swear!
If he gets away, everything we just did was for nothing! We almost DIED out there! Just grab him!
Rain pulled out a rope and moved toward the mercenary, but you stepped in front of her, blocking her path.
Get out of my way. Do NOT test me right now. I swear if you—
A single shot. The mercenary dropped.

...What? You two were too busy arguing. If he escapes, he tells the Empire about the system and the Heavy Armor. Our mission fails. If the mission fails, I do not get promoted. If I do not get promoted, my family does not eat. I am not taking that risk.
Well, at least this one does not have to worry about the noose anymore.
Badol turned and walked toward the other fallen mercenaries. Another shot. Then another.
narration_mercenary_ambush: Alright, before you head out, make sure you secure the Heavy Armor during transport. The desert route can be—
A shot rang out. The officer collapsed mid-sentence. Then another. And another.
The officers! They are all hit!
Mercenaries! No insignias, no uniforms. These are not Imperial soldiers.
They are here for the Guysack! Get behind it, now! It is the only cover we have!
Our Zoids are right there! We need to get to them!
Are you crazy?! That is open ground! They will pick us off before we take three steps!
Listen to me. Both of you. Grab the officers' rifles. I will go first. Once I reach my Viper, I will cover you from there. When I start shooting, you run. Got it?
Rain, you will be completely exposed!
I am the fastest one here. Just be ready to move when I say so.
Rain grabbed a rifle and broke from cover. She sprinted across the open ground, firing as she ran. The mercenaries scrambled between returning fire and taking cover from her shots.
She reached the Stealth Viper. Climbed in. The Viper's guns roared to life, pinning the mercenaries down.
narration_rain_pressure: That should be enough. The transmitters are in place, the Heavy Armor is set up below. All that is left is for you to activate the system.
What is the holdup? We have been at this for hours. Just activate it.
What is wrong with you? Why do you keep stalling?
You know... before all this, they were living things. Now they are just antennas. Receivers. Following a signal until someone puts them down. Not much of a life, is it.
Oh, not you too. What is this, a funeral? They are machines!
I am just saying what we are all thinking. Well, what he is thinking.
narration_reconciliation: ...the Republic is losing this war, Kara. If we lose, an army that is not even from this continent will decide everything for us. They would never do this if they had a choice. None of us should be here. You, me, him. I am a child commanding soldiers. He is using Zoids as weapons against their nature. None of this is right.
Then why do you accept it?
Because if the Republic wins, at least we have a chance. A chance to try to change things. That is all any of us want. To end this war and have a say in what comes after.
You love Zoids too, Mana. I have seen how you talk to them. How can you be okay with turning them into... that?
I am not okay with it. None of us are. But I would rather fight to end this war and then fix what we broke, than lose and never get the chance.
...I think someone is here for you. You two have things to work out. I will leave you to it.
...She told me everything. That you did not want to do it. That you hated every second of it. Is that true? You felt the same way I did this whole time?
Then promise me something. When this war is over... you will free them. All of them. The Sleepers in those ruins. You will give them back what my father wanted for them.
She also told me... about how you refused to activate the system. How much it was hurting you. She made me promise not to tell you she was here, so... keep it between us, okay?
I think Rain wanted me to forgive you. But she was also... different. I do not know what you two went through in those ruins, but it changed her too.
...I am still angry. But I believe you. Do not make me regret it.
narration_ruins_cleared: Alright, we need to push deeper. Clear out the Imperial Sleepers and find a good spot to set up the Heavy Armor as the signal source.
Ha! Did you see that one? It did not even see me coming. I could do this all day.
Careful, Rain. You are starting to enjoy this a little too much.
What is not to enjoy? Smashing Imperial junk is the best part of this job. You better watch out, big guy. I am starting to like destroying Sleepers. Yours might be next.
Keep moving. We still have a lot of ground to cover.
narration_sea_panther_appears: That was the last of them. Is everyone alright?
I am fine. Nice shooting out there, Rain.
Save the compliments for later. Something is not right. That was too easy for a planned ambush.
A Sea Panther emerged from behind the depot, heading straight for the Guysack Heavy Armor.
That must be their leader! He is going for the Heavy Armor!
We are too far! The snipers pulled us away from the depot! We will never make it back in time!
Your Sleepers! They are still near the Heavy Armor! They are the only ones close enough! Use them!
narration_sleeper_aftermath: The Stealth Viper hit the ground. The Sleepers stopped firing. For a moment, everything was silent. Then they started moving. Slowly. All of them. Closing in from every direction.
What are they doing?! Call them off! CALL THEM OFF!
One of the Sleepers lunged forward, grabbed the Viper by the neck and started squeezing. The Stealth Viper let out a high-pitched shriek, its metal frame buckling and grinding under the pressure.
NO! Stop it! You are going to crush her! LET HER GO!
Please! She did nothing wrong! It was me! I was the one shooting! Take it out on me, not on her!
You are hurting her... please... I get it... I am sorry...
The Sleeper released its grip. The Stealth Viper collapsed to the ground, dented and whimpering. The Sleepers returned to their positions as if nothing had happened.
For junk, they sure bite hard, huh?
Uh... guys? The fight must have alerted the Sleepers we installed. We should get out of here before they decide we do not belong.
narration_sleeper_confrontation: How much longer are we going to have to wait for you?! Just activate the system!
Hey, easy. Understand that this is hard for him. He controls them, he knows them. It is not the same for him as it is for you and me.
Hard?! Hard is losing your family because the Empire took everything from you! This is just pressing a button!
What? You are going to face me now? You would rather fight me than do your job?
You hide behind your Sleepers to earn your place in the army, but when you can actually use them to save lives, you do not have the nerve?! You are a fraud and a coward!
Fine! If you care so much about them, let me show you what they really are!
What the— Rain! Stop shooting! Those are HIS Sleepers! Are you out of your mind?!
See?! Junk! They are just junk that cannot even dodge a shot! They will never be the same as a piloted Zoid! Never!
training_officer_ruins_briefing: Listen up. Intelligence has detected Imperial activity near the ancient ruins to the north. Scout patrols, reconnaissance teams. They think we have not noticed. We are going to keep it that way.

We have been working on something new. A way to make our Sleepers... more effective. No more Zoids sitting around waiting to be stepped on. This time, when the Empire walks into those ruins, they will not walk out.

You are on this mission because you have the most experience with Sleepers. Rain, you were the first to complete the trials. You are the most capable recruit we have. Decisive, the mission crosses the desert. Your survival skills will be essential out there.

First, head to the supply depot at the Abandoned Camp. You will receive the full briefing and pick up the equipment there. After that, the ruins. Clear out the Imperial Sleepers and set up our new system.
training_officer_ruins_debrief: I have received your field report. The Sleeper network is operational. Good work.
I also read about the mercenary attack at the depot. We are looking into who hired them, though I think we all know the answer.
You three handled a situation that would have broken most veteran squads. That speaks well of you.
Get some rest. You have earned it.
